name: Can a small kitchen have an island?

mainEntity.name: Can a small kitchen in a Los Angeles home still have an island after a layout change?
mainEntity.text: Can a small kitchen in a Los Angeles home still have an island after a layout change?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small kitchen can sometimes include an island, but the space must be measured carefully. The island should not interrupt circulation or make cabinet and appliance doors difficult to use. In many smaller Los Angeles kitchens, a compact island is possible if the room is reconfigured intelligently and unnecessary barriers are removed. In others, a peninsula or smaller prep surface is the better choice because it adds function without overcrowding the room. The key question is not whether an island is trendy, but whether it improves the actual workflow. If it creates a pinch point, it will feel like a mistake every day. A good design should consider how many people use the kitchen, whether kids or guests pass through it, and how much storage is already available. Small kitchens often benefit more from clever storage, better lighting, and tighter planning than from forcing in a large island.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only if there is enough clearance for safe movement and appliance doors. In very small kitchens, a full island can make the room feel tighter, so a smaller island, peninsula, or movable prep table may work better.
